research_vector: APP STORE ARCHAEOLOGY - Legacy Apps Still Ranking Despite Years Without Updates

key_findings.abandoned_app_prevalence: As of Q3 2024, 682,000+ apps on Apple App Store are abandoned (not updated in 2+ years). 51% of all App Store apps haven't been updated in 1+ year.
key_findings.apple_policy: Apps not updated in 3+ years that fail minimal download threshold receive removal notices. Apps over 1 year old with no updates get 90-day update requirement.
key_findings.paradox: Many abandoned apps continue getting significant downloads and positive ratings, suggesting user loyalty to 'feature complete' apps.

apps.name: Flappy Bird
apps.status: Removed 2014, revival announced 2024 by Gametech Holdings (unauthorized)
apps.original_creator_stance: Dong Nguyen disavows 2024 revival - 'no relation with their game'

apps.trademark_history: Creator lost trademark rights due to abandonment claim; Gametech Holdings acquired

apps.current_status: Developers created Ivory (Mastodon client) as successor

apps.name: Twitterrific

business_implications.opportunity: Abandoned apps with high ratings and active downloads represent market gaps for replacement/improvement
business_implications.risk: Privacy and security concerns as abandoned apps don't receive security patches
business_implications.platform_response: Apple enforces 3-year update policy; Google Play more lenient but increasing enforcement
business_implications.developer_dilemma: Maintenance costs vs. revenue from legacy apps often lead to abandonment
